clue.text: Coppers put to death entering church

definitions.note: plural sense: copper coins are small change, so the noun stands for loose coins

indicators.note: the execution verb goes into the church letters, so entering signals one piece placed inside another

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
to hang is to execute by the rope

explanation.surface: Police officers carrying out an execution inside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: Coppers looks like police, but it means copper coins. CE is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Coppers are low-value coins, and small coins collectively are loose money in the pocket.

clue.text: Sophisticated type of loco

indicators.note: a type of loco is read as a version of its letters rearranged into another form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Describing a smart, refined kind of railway engine.
explanation.definitionFit: Cool in its informal sense means stylish, fashionable and urbane, which is a synonym of sophisticated.

clue.text: Julie, the singer, wanders around

indicators.note: the letters of wanders are moved around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A performer named Julie strolls about aimlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Julie Andrews is the English singer and actress famous for Mary Poppins and The Sound of Music.

clue.text: Talented star's reputation

parts.note: a talented performer is good at it
a star is a big name, and the possessive is read as star is

explanation.surface: A gifted celebrity's standing in public opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s in star's is read as 'star is', the star being a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's good name is their honour or standing in others' eyes, an idiom for reputation.

clue.text: Most drivelling GI has assets all over the place

indicators.note: scattered in disorder, so the letters of GI and assets are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American soldier talks nonsense while his possessions lie scattered.
explanation.definitionFit: Gassy means full of empty talk or hot air, so the superlative describes the windiest, most talkative speaker.

clue.text: Criminal's helpers approach leaderless Tories

parts.note: access is a way in, an approach to a place

indicators.note: the Tories lose their leader, the first letter of the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Accomplices of a crook draw near to a Conservative party with no leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Tories are members of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: In law an accessory is someone who assists a crime, before or after the fact, without being the main perpetrator.

clue.text: Short, thick agent holding stomach

indicators.note: the agent's letters hold the stomach's letters between them

parts.note: a secret agent is a spy
tum is the informal word for stomach

explanation.surface: A squat secret agent clutching his belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Stumpy describes something short and stubby, like a stump, so it means short and thickset.

clue.text: Model boy tucked into the end of the sausage pie

indicators.note: only the final letter of sausage is taken

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the boy's name is placed inside the word pie

parts.note: taken as written
Tom is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad digs into the last bit of a sausage pie.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is a perfect example or embodiment of something, which is what a model of a type is.

clue.text: Change found on bar where records are played

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: to turn is to change, as leaves turn colour
a bar, like a table, is a flat counter for serving at

explanation.surface: Coins left on a pub counter beside the jukebox.
explanation.walkthrough: Change looks like loose coins found on a pub counter; here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A turntable is the rotating platform of a record player on which vinyl discs spin.

clue.text: Former pupil getting on by hiding ring

parts.note: someone getting on in years is old

indicators.note: the word by hides the ring shape inside it

parts.note: taken as written
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: An alumnus doing well while concealing a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: An old boy is a former student of a school, used especially of British public schools.

clue.text: See inhabitant turn up embracing a tart

indicators.note: the letters for turn up surround the tart's letters

parts.note: to occur is to happen or turn up
a tart is a kind of pie

explanation.surface: A resident arrives carrying a pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: See is a link word, the setter telling the solver to look; it also hints at a bishop occupying a see.
explanation.definitionFit: An occupier is a person living in or holding a property, which makes them its resident.

clue.text: Resources of the underwear department?

parts.note: the straight sense: money or income one lives on
the playful sense: bras and corsets literally hold things up

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for income or livelihood is read literally as the garments that support the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Means of support is an idiom for one's livelihood or income, and supportive lingerie fits it literally.

clue.text: Show a number in love position

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

indicators.note: the number sits inside the word for position

parts.note: a station is a post or position
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Displaying a numeral in the love position.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostentation is a pretentious display meant to impress, so it is a showing-off.

clue.text: August feast, in theory

definitions.meaning: first sense: the church feast of Mary taken into heaven, on 15 August
second sense: a supposition taken for granted

explanation.walkthrough: The word in is a link joining the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the Catholic holy day on 15 August and an unproven supposition or premise.

clue.text: What's passed on cleans tar off

indicators.note: the letters are set off course, rearranged out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An inherited tip: a cleaning method that removes tar.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestral describes things inherited from forebears, handed down the generations as heirlooms are.

clue.text: Mint, perhaps, is found in another bed

indicators.note: the answer's letters are found sitting inside the run of words another bed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener finds mint growing in a different flowerbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Mint is an example of a culinary plant used for flavouring, which is what the answer names.

clue.text: Being hard working, I cover up information on time

indicators.note: in a down clue the earlier piece sits on top of the next
in a down clue the word is written upwards, reading backwards

parts.note: a lid covers a pot
taken as written
gen is British slang for information
T

explanation.surface: A conscientious worker hiding inside information about timing.
explanation.walkthrough: Cover up looks like conceal; it is a cover written upwards. Being is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Diligent means industrious and painstaking, a synonym of hard working.

clue.text: Approximately one bollard

parts.note: c, for circa, means approximately before a date
taken as written

explanation.surface: Roughly a single traffic bollard.
explanation.definitionFit: A traffic cone is a portable plastic marker used on roads, much as a bollard is.

clue.text: Portia's waiting-maid held up as femme fatale

indicators.note: in a down clue the words are lifted up, so they read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
a siren is a dangerously seductive woman

explanation.surface: A lady's maid is delayed, playing a seductress.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice, Nerissa is the attendant who serves the heiress Portia.

clue.text: Look forward to captain getting tie twisted

indicators.note: the letters of captain and tie are twisted out of shape into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A captain eagerly awaits having his necktie twisted.
explanation.definitionFit: To anticipate something is to expect it, as with looking forward to an event.

clue.text: A great distance keeps a sailor good tempered

indicators.note: the first letters keep the sailor's letters held inside them

parts.note: taken as written
a mile is a long way
AB, an able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor far off still keeps his good humour.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiable means friendly and pleasant in manner, close to good-natured.

clue.text: Lemony fruit: an old woman nearly squeezes it

indicators.note: the shortened word squeezes the other letters inside
nearly the whole word: its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a crone is an old woman
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old lady almost squeezing a lemon.
explanation.definitionFit: A citron is a large citrus fruit like a lemon, with thick rind used for candied peel.

clue.text: I am a hospital cleaner

parts.note: the riddle form: the answer speaks of itself, inviting a person
looks like a ward cleaner, but means an antiseptic liquid

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a cleaning worker; the answer is the alcohol-based fluid used in hospitals to sterilise skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgical spirit is a methylated alcohol used medically to disinfect skin and instruments.

clue.text: One carried in thirsty brewer's cart

indicators.note: the one is carried inside the word for thirsty

parts.note: dry means thirsty
a is one

explanation.surface: A single man is taken on a cart to a parched brewer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dray is a low flat cart without sides, traditionally used by brewers to deliver beer barrels.

clue.text: Have time off before taking rain check

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the second, which it takes on behind it

parts.note: to rest is to take a break
taken as written

explanation.surface: Take a break before accepting a rain check.
explanation.walkthrough: Rain check looks like a phrase; check is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to hold it back or curb it, synonymous with restraining it.

clue.text: I belong to a group: remember the first two are missing

definitions.note: a sentence the answer speaks: the noun for one who belongs

indicators.note: the opening two letters of remember are gone

parts.note: taken as written, a whole word whose opening is cut away

explanation.surface: A forgetful person reminding themself they are part of a club.
explanation.definitionFit: A member is one who belongs to a club, society or other body.

clue.text: Tendency to hold right scholarship

indicators.note: the tendency word holds the letter for right inside it

parts.note: a leaning is an inclination or tendency

explanation.surface: A propensity to retain the proper academic award.
explanation.walkthrough: Scholarship suggests a grant, but here it means erudition.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholarship in its sense of erudition is the knowledge gained through study, i.e. learning.

clue.text: Bluish-grey fish where the pig should be

parts.note: a pig belongs in a sty, its pen
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A grey-blue fish turns up in a pigsty.
explanation.walkthrough: The fish placed in the pig's place is read as fish inside the pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Steely describes the bluish-grey colour of steel metal.
